text_en: Three days after Festus had arrived in the province, he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem
text_cn: 斐斯托到省上任，三天以后，就从凯撒勒雅上了耶路撒冷。

text_en: where the chief priests and the leaders of the Jews gave him a report against Paul. They appealed to him
text_cn: 司祭长和犹太人的首领，向他告发保禄，并请求他开恩，

text_en: and requested, as a favor to them against Paul, to have him transferred to Jerusalem. They were, in fact, planning an ambush to kill him along the way.
text_cn: 来对付保禄，就是求他将保禄解到耶路撒冷来，他们好设下埋伏，在半路上将他杀掉。

text_en: Festus replied that Paul was being kept at Caesarea, and that he himself intended to go there shortly.
text_cn: 可是，斐斯托回答说：“保禄应押在凯撒勒雅，我自己不久就快回去；”

text_en: “So, ” he said, “let those of you who have the authority come down with me, and if there is anything wrong about the man, let them accuse him. ”
text_cn: 又说：“你们中有权势的人，跟我一同下去，若在那人身上有什么不对处，控告他好了。”

text_en: After he had stayed among them not more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea; the next day he took his seat on the tribunal and ordered Paul to be brought.
text_cn: 斐斯托在他们中住了不过八天或十天，就下到了凯撒勒雅。第二天坐堂，下令将保禄带来；

text_en: When he arrived, the Jews who had gone down from Jerusalem surrounded him, bringing many serious charges against him, which they could not prove.
text_cn: 保禄一来到，从耶路撒冷下来的犹太人就围住他，提出许多严重而不能证明的罪状。

text_en: Paul said in his defense, “I have in no way committed an offense against the law of the Jews, or against the temple, or against the emperor. ”
text_cn: 保禄分辩说：“我对于犹太人的法律，对于圣殿，对于凯撒，都没有犯什么罪。”

text_en: But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, asked Paul, “Do you wish to go up to Jerusalem and be tried there before me on these charges? ”
text_cn: 斐斯托想要向犹太人讨好，就向保禄说：“关于这些事，你愿意上耶路撒冷，在那里于我面前受审吗？”

text_en: Paul said, “I am appealing to the emperor’s tribunal; this is where I should be tried. I have done no wrong to the Jews, as you very well know.
text_cn: 保禄却说：“我站在凯撒的公堂前，我该在这里受审。我对犹太人并没有作过不对的事，就是你也知道的很清楚。

text_en: Now if I am in the wrong and have committed something for which I deserve to die, I am not trying to escape death; but if there is nothing to their charges against me, no one can turn me over to them. I appeal to the emperor. ”
text_cn: 假如我作了不对的事，或作了什么该死的事，我虽死不辞；但若这些人所控告我的，都是实无其事，那么谁也不能将我交与他们；我向凯撒上诉。”

text_en: Then Festus, after he had conferred with his council, replied, “You have appealed to the emperor; to the emperor you will go. ”
text_cn: 斐斯托与议会商议之后，回答说：“你既向凯撒上诉，就往凯撒那里去！”

text_en: After several days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to welcome Festus.
text_cn: 过了几天，阿格黎帕王同贝勒尼切到了凯撒勒雅，向斐斯托致候。

text_en: Since they were staying there several days, Festus laid Paul’s case before the king, saying, “There is a man here who was left in prison by Felix.
text_cn: 他们在那里住了多日，斐斯托就将保禄的事件，陈述给王说：“这里有一个人，是斐理斯留在狱中的囚犯。

text_en: When I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews informed me about him and asked for a sentence against him.
text_cn: 我在耶路撒冷的时候，司祭长和犹太人的长老告发他，要求定他的罪。

text_en: I told them that it was not the custom of the Romans to hand over anyone before the accused had met the accusers face to face and had been given an opportunity to make a defense against the charge.
text_cn: 我回答他们说：当被告还没有与原告当面对质，还没有机会辩护控告他的事以前，就将那人交出，不合罗马人的规例。

text_en: So when they met here, I lost no time, but on the next day took my seat on the tribunal and ordered the man to be brought.
text_cn: 及至他们来到这里，我一点也没有迟延，次日便坐堂，下令把那人带来。

text_en: When the accusers stood up, they did not charge him with any of the crimes that I was expecting.
text_cn: 原告站起来，对他没有提出一件罪案，是我所逆料的恶事；

text_en: Instead they had certain points of disagreement with him about their own religion and about a certain Jesus, who had died, but whom Paul asserted to be alive.
text_cn: 他们的争辩，仅是关于他们的宗教及关于一个已死的耶稣，保禄却说他还活着。

text_en: Since I was at a loss how to investigate these questions, I asked whether he wished to go to Jerusalem and be tried there on these charges.
text_cn: 我对这争执不知如何处理，就问他是否愿意去耶路撒冷，在那里受审。

text_en: But when Paul had appealed to be kept in custody for the decision of his Imperial Majesty, I ordered him to be held until I could send him to the emperor. ”
text_cn: 可是，保禄却要求上诉，将他留给皇帝审断，我便下令留下他，等我解他到凯撒那里。”

text_en: Agrippa said to Festus, “I would like to hear the man myself. ” “Tomorrow, ” he said, “you will hear him. ”
text_cn: 阿格黎帕向斐斯托说：“我也愿意亲自听听这个人。”斐斯托说：“明天你就可以听他。”

text_en: So on the next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp, and they entered the audience hall with the military tribunes and the prominent men of the city. Then Festus gave the order and Paul was brought in.
text_cn: 第二天，阿格黎帕和贝勒尼切来时甚是排场，偕同千夫长及城里的要人进了厅堂；斐斯托下令，把保禄带来。

text_en: And Festus said, “King Agrippa and all here present with us, you see this man about whom the whole Jewish community petitioned me, both in Jerusalem and here, shouting that he ought not to live any longer.
text_cn: 斐斯托说：“阿格黎帕王和同我们在场的众人，你们看这个人，为了他，所有的犹太群众曾在耶路撒冷和这里向我请求，呼喊说：不该容他再活下去。

text_en: But I found that he had done nothing deserving death; and when he appealed to his Imperial Majesty, I decided to send him.
text_cn: 但我查明他并没有作过什么该死的事。他既把这案子向皇帝上诉了，我便决定把他解去。

text_en: But I have nothing definite to write to our sovereign about him. Therefore I have brought him before all of you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that, after we have examined him, I may have something to write—
text_cn: 我对这人没有什么确实的事可向主上陈奏； 因此我将他带到你们前，尤其你阿格黎帕王前，好在审讯以后，有所陈奏，

text_en: for it seems to me unreasonable to send a prisoner without indicating the charges against him. ”
text_cn: 因为我以为，解送囚犯而不指明他的罪状，于理不合。”
